data.name: PanelToolTip
data.value: Scripts, commands from DLLs, the console.

data.name: PanelDescription
data.value: Tools for add-in developers. Script Editor runs C# scripts right in Revit, Add-in Explorer runs commands from built DLLs without restarting Revit and shows the ribbon, the start-up add-ins and DLL version conflicts. Repeat Last repeats the last run, Console shows the output.

data.name: ScriptEditorToolTip
data.value: C# script editor.

data.name: ScriptEditorDescription
data.value: Write code right in Revit and run it without rebuilding an add-in. All the output, Console.WriteLine, Debug and exceptions, goes to the add-in's console.

data.name: ExplorerToolTip
data.value: Add-ins and their DLLs: commands, ribbon, start-up, conflicts.

data.name: ExplorerDescription
data.value: Add a built DLL and run an IExternalCommand from it: the command comes from the DLL on disk as it is now. It also shows how an add-in's ribbon will change, which add-ins Revit loads at start-up and which DLLs they have in different versions.

data.name: RepeatToolTip
data.value: Repeat the last script or command from a DLL.

data.name: RepeatDescription
data.value: A command from a DLL is taken from the file on disk, so after a rebuild the new version runs. A script is repeated as it was run; edits in the editor apply after F5.

data.name: DebugToolTip
data.value: Repeat the last command under the Visual Studio debugger.

data.name: DebugDescription
data.value: Repeats the last command from Add-in Explorer with the open Visual Studio attached: breakpoints set in the project are hit. Visual Studio must be open with the add-in's solution. Scripts are debugged in Script Editor, with the bug button.

data.name: ConsoleToolTip
data.value: Show or hide the console.

data.name: ConsoleDescription
data.value: The output of scripts and commands from DLLs goes here: Console.WriteLine, Debug, Trace and exceptions. The checkboxes in its header set what happens to the console and the views before each run.
